problem: Direct language-to-action mapping in VLA models for quadruped robots gives weak interpretability and unstable grounding, while latent intermediate embeddings hide the semantic logic and prevent compositional reasoning and error tracing. Prior VLN/VLA methods struggle to bridge high-level semantic reasoning with low-level continuous actuation.
motivation: Service and assistive robots need to follow natural-language instructions reliably in real environments, which requires interpretable planning coupled with stable control. Explicit chain-of-thought reasoning, aligned with SFT and refined with GRPO-style RL, is expected to improve reasoning consistency, control stability and long-horizon execution.
key_idea: Generate structured <think>/<answer> CoT plans that are parsed into continuous velocity plus discrete actions for a quadruped, training with SFT on a synthesized multi-granularity CoT dataset followed by GRPO with movement, action and format rewards.
insight: Each of the three GRPO rewards contributes complementary signal: on R2R-CE val-unseen SR rises from 58.0 (SFT-only) to 68.3 with all rewards, and any pair is worse (64.5 to 65.2). Adding depth and point-cloud encoders to the RGB baseline raises R2R-CE SR from 62.5 to 68.3, showing that 3D perception helps. Caveat: the 8B model has about 10 s per decision step, so it is only usable in quasi-static scenes.
method: MobileVLA-CoT dataset: Gemini-2.5-Flash generates <think>/<answer> annotations from RGB-D, instructions and state-action histories on R2R/RxR/QUARD train splits, giving Episode-level (18K), Step-level (78K) and Nav-level (38K) CoT, filtered by rules plus manual review.

Multimodal architecture: LLaVA-style model initialized from NaVILA (LLaMA3-8B); adds a DepthAnything V2 depth encoder and Point Transformer v3 point-cloud encoder, fused by a lightweight projection; vision encoders frozen and LoRA (r=16, alpha=32) on the LLM.
Action formulation: the policy outputs a_t=[Vx,Vy,w_yaw,alpha], continuous velocities plus a discrete high-level action, deterministically parsed from the <answer> tag.
Cold-start SFT: train on full CoT-Episode and CoT-Nav (about 20K steps) then a 10K subset of CoT-Step, to learn the format and reasoning-to-command mapping (4xH20, lr 2e-4).
GRPO reinforcement learning: 8 samples per prompt, 1K steps, lr 1e-6, beta=0.04, clip 0.2, with a KL penalty to the SFT reference.
Reward design: movement reward (cosine similarity of predicted and GT velocity vectors), binary action reward on the discrete action, and binary format reward for the <think><answer> template.
Deployment: Unitree Go2 with L2 LiDAR and RealSense D435i; inference runs on a remote H20 server that sends velocity commands back to the robot.

setting.backbone: NaVILA-initialized LLaVA-style VLM with LLaMA3-8B, DepthAnything V2 and PTv3 encoders (LoRA SFT + GRPO)
setting.training_data: MobileVLA-CoT synthesized from R2R, RxR and QUARD train splits (Episode 18K, Step 78K (10K subset used in SFT), Nav 38K), plus the NaVILA initialization
setting.action_space: continuous velocities (Vx, Vy, yaw rate) plus a discrete high-level action
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE on Matterport3D); QUARD benchmark; real Unitree Go2

numbers_note: Real-world Go2 results (Table 4) are on custom setups, not benchmark splits, so they are not listed as numbers. Example Workspace-Simple: NE 1.03, SR 0.93; Corridor-Simple SR 1.00; Outdoor-Complex SR 0.96.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen it reaches SR 68.3 / SPL 65.2, beating CorrectNav (65.1 / 62.3) and StreamVLN (56.9 / 51.9). On RxR-CE it reaches SR 71.5 vs CorrectNav 69.3. On QUARD the average is 0.73 vs 0.60 for MoRE, and it beats NaVILA and GPT-4o in real-world Go2 tests.
limitations: Latency is high: about 10 s per decision step and about 15 s end-to-end on a remote H20 server, so it suits only quasi-static scenes.
Action decoding maps to a fixed set of predefined behaviors, and training relies on supervised, semi-scripted data with Gemini-generated CoT.
Its SOTA comparison uses extra depth and point-cloud inputs that most baselines lack, and the real-world evaluation has few trials and no stated episode counts.
